title: Ginkgetin Attenuates Dextran Sulfate Sodium-Induced Colitis by Inhibiting the Nuclear Factor Kappa B Pathway.
authors: Qiao, Xuejing; Xie, Wei; Ding, Yanfei; Shan, Lianmei
one_liner_zh: 研究银杏双黄酮通过抑制NF-κB通路缓解结肠炎，涉及p65蛋白互作但非DNA结合，且以湿实验为主，与本课题TF-DNA互作建模无关。
abstract: Ginkgetin is a biflavone isolated from Ginkgo biloba leaves. It has shown anti-inflammatory effects in colitis. However, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the therapeutic effects of ginkgetin on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-treated Caco-2 cells. Inflammation, the integrity of the colonic epithelial barrier, and cellular damage were assessed via immunofluorescence, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting. Furthermore, p65 was overexpressed or knocked down to examine its involvement in the observed effects. Treatment with ginkgetin significantly attenuated weight loss, disease activity index, and histopathological damage in DSS-induced mice. It also downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), and interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta), and upregulated tight junction proteins, such as zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) and Occludin, in vivo and in vitro. Notably, ginkgetin inhibited p-p65 and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2 in colonic tissues and Caco-2 cells. Molecular docking, biotin pull-down, and cellular thermal shift assays suggested an interaction between ginkgetin and p65. p65 overexpression reversed the inhibitory effects of ginkgetin on LPS-induced inflammation and barrier disruption. p65 knockdown normalized LPS-induced alterations, downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, and IL-1beta), and upregulated tight junction proteins (ZO-1 and Occludin). Notably, the addition of ginkgetin did not further improve the beneficial effects of p65 knockdown alone. These findings suggest that ginkgetin alleviated colitis by modulating inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction through the nuclear factor kappa B pathway. This study demonstrates the potential of ginkgetin as a therapeutic agent for colitis.
abstract_zh: 银杏素（Ginkgetin）是从银杏叶中分离出的一种双黄酮类化合物，在结肠炎中显示出抗炎作用。然而，其分子机制尚不清楚。本研究探讨了银杏素对葡聚糖硫酸钠（DSS）诱导的小鼠结肠炎及脂多糖（LPS）处理的Caco-2细胞的治疗作用。通过免疫荧光、逆转录定量聚合酶链反应和蛋白质印迹法评估炎症、结肠上皮屏障完整性及细胞损伤。此外，通过过表达或敲低p65来检验其在观察效应中的作用。银杏素治疗显著减轻了DSS诱导小鼠的体重下降、疾病活动指数及组织病理损伤。在体内和体外实验中，它还下调了促炎细胞因子，如白细胞介素-6（IL-6）、肿瘤坏死因子-α（TNF-α）和白细胞介素-1β（IL-1β），并上调了紧密连接蛋白，如闭锁小带蛋白-1（ZO-1）和Occludin。值得注意的是，银杏素抑制了结肠组织和Caco-2细胞中的p-p65及C-X-C基序趋化因子配体2。分子对接、生物素下拉和细胞热位移实验提示银杏素与p65之间存在相互作用。p65过表达逆转了银杏素对LPS诱导的炎症和屏障破坏的抑制作用。p65敲低使LPS诱导的变化恢复正常，下调了促炎细胞因子（IL-6、TNF-α和IL-1β），并上调了紧密连接蛋白（ZO-1和Occludin）。值得注意的是，添加银杏素并未进一步改善单独p65敲低的有益效果。这些发现表明，银杏素通过核因子κB通路调节炎症和上皮屏障功能障碍，从而缓解结肠炎。本研究展示了银杏素作为结肠炎治疗药物的潜力。
